entities.summary: Leo Ernest Durocher, nicknamed "Leo the Lip" and "Lippy", was an American professional baseball player, manager, and coach. He played in Major League Baseball (MLB) as an infielder. Upon his retirement, he ranked fifth all-time among managers with 2,008 career victories, second only to John McGraw in National League history. Durocher still ranks twelfth in career wins by a manager. A controversial and outspoken character, Durocher's half-century in baseball was dogged by clashes with authority, the baseball commissioner, the press, and umpires; his 100 career ejections as a manager trailed only McGraw when he retired, and he still ranks third on the all-time list.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the most successful managers in MLB history with 2,008 career victories, Leo Durocher's impact on baseball was significant, ranking him twelfth all-time among managers. His 100 career ejections trail only John McGraw when he retired.
